about: Hiruzta sits at the foot of Mount Jaizkibel in Hondarribia, the walled Basque town on the French border that gave the Hondarrabi Zuri grape its name. Records show txakoli made here as early as the twelfth century, but the tradition died out during the sieges of the 1600s. In the late 2000s Asensio Rekalde and his sons Txarli and Ángel set out to bring it back. The winery’s name means “a harvest of three” in Basque. Their winery stands on the site of an old quarry, and the estate includes a grill restaurant.

The estate’s 11 hectares of vines face south across Txingudi Bay, sheltered by Jaizkibel from the damp Cantabrian winds. The vines grow in clay-marl soils over bedrock and are trained on wires in the double Guyot system. The white is made mostly or entirely from Hondarrabi Zuri, picked by hand, fermented cool and rested on its fine lees for several months. A little natural carbon dioxide is kept for the faint prickle typical of Getariako Txakolina.

The winery describes pear, apple, grapefruit and passion fruit with a hint of orange blossom, and a crisp, citrusy palate. Decanter rated the 2022 at 90 points for its riper melon-and-peach style, lemon-peel nose and delicate spritz. James Suckling, tasting the 2021, found chalk, lime and nectarine. In Hondarribia it is poured with anchovy pintxos, and the winery names oysters as one of its best matches.
facts: Hondarrabi Zuri (some vintages include about 5% Gros Manseng)
11 ha estate below Mount Jaizkibel; clay marl over bedrock; double Guyot
Hand harvested; cool fermentation; aged on its lees; light natural spritz
